currents.source: DocID027107 Rev 6 (STM32F446xC/E, Sep 2016; a mirror copy, ST's current DS10693 not read): run 180 MHz from flash, external clock, PLL on, all peripherals disabled 32 mA typ (72 mA all enabled), 25 °C (Table 23); Stop with the low-power regulator, flash in Stop mode 0.15 mA typ (0.121 mA flash in deep power-down; under-drive lower) (Table 27). No minimum supply current stated; 150 mA is Bringup's margin

history.source: STM32duino EEPROM emulation on F4: FLASH_PAGE_SIZE 8 KB in the last flash sector, and the whole sector (128 KB on these parts) is erased on each write-back (framework-arduinoststm32 4.21200 libraries/EEPROM/src/utility/stm32_eeprom.h)

sim.note: Renode 1.17 has stm32f4 (an F407) and stm32f412 platforms, not the F446

motion.source: grblHAL Drivers README (github.com/grblHAL/Drivers, read 14 Nov 2026): STM32F4xx in the 'With floating point unit (FPU)' table, boards 'Blackpill / Nucleo-F411RE / Nucleo-F446RE'; Cortex-M4F single-precision FPU (DocID027107 §1: Arm Cortex-M4 with FPU)

sources: DocID027107 Rev 6 (Sep 2016): Table 18 VCAP_1 4.7 µF ESR < 1 Ω with a single VCAP pin (LQFP64 has only VCAP_1), power supply scheme (VDD n × 100 nF + 4.7 µF), boot modes (BOOT0 low: flash)

No crystal: STM32duino's generic F446RE clock (variants/STM32F4xx/F446R(C-E)T/generic_clock.c) runs from the HSI. nucleo_f446re isn't used: a Nucleo takes its clock from the ST-LINK, which a Bringup board doesn't have. USB OTG FS needs an HSE, so the profile has no usb and the board doesn't wire it
Console USART1 on PA9/PA10: the pins ST's ROM bootloader also listens on (AN2606)
